subject: math
verificationNotes: Hand-authored; numeric answers checked with sympy.
intro: To compare two or more distributions, address shape, center, spread, and unusual features for each, and state comparisons in context (not just side-by-side numbers). Side-by-side boxplots and back-to-back stemplots make comparison easy. Always use comparative language ('Group A has a higher median than Group B') and mention overlap and outliers.

items.prompt: Group A has median $70$, Group B has median $82$. Compare centers.

steps: Both summaries describe the center with the median.
Compare: $82>70$, so Group B's typical value is higher.
In context: Group B tends to score higher than Group A.
solution.answer: Group B has the higher center (median $82>70$).

items.prompt: Group A has IQR $5$, Group B has IQR $15$. Compare spread.

steps: IQR measures the spread of the middle half.
$15>5$, so Group B is more variable.
In context: Group B's values are more spread out than Group A's.

items.prompt: Boxplot A is symmetric; boxplot B has a long upper whisker. Compare shape.

steps: A symmetric box suggests a symmetric distribution.
A long upper whisker indicates right skew for B.
So A is roughly symmetric while B is skewed right.
Same center; the second group is less variable.
solution.answer: Equal centers; second group less spread.

items.prompt: Which group is more consistent: IQR $3$ or IQR $9$?
A boxplot with the median line near the left of the box suggests what skew?

steps: Longer right side means right skew.
